newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian refinery to overcome water problem soon.
newsitem.headline: Indian refinery to overcome water problem soon.

text.p: Indian state-owned oil refiner Cochin Refineries Ltd is expected to restore water supply to its refinery within the next two days to enable resumption of operations, company and state officials said on Tuesday.

"I think within the next two days the immediate problem should be resolved," Annamma (one name), an official with the Irrigation department in the southern state of Kerala told Reuters by telephone from Cochin.

"Due to low voltage we cannot pump out enough water to meet the high demand of the refinery so we have called a meeting with the refinery's management and the state electricity board, after which the immediate supply should start," Annamma said.
A company spokesman said restart of the refinery would depend on when the authorities were able to resume water supplies.
"The shut down is only for a short time... it will be solved in a day or two," he said.
The 150,000-barrel-per-day refinery, located on the southwest cost of India, has an annual capacity of 7.5 million metric tonnes.
Annamma said the supply pipes to the refinery needed replacement as the existing ones were unable to take the heavy water pressure needed to supply the refinery units.
The department wanted the refinery to pay for changing the pipes.
"They (the refinery) have to pay for the cost of the maintenence and replacement of pipes but they are not prepared to give the money," she said.
"The replacement will cost around 70.0 million rupees and the water authority does not have the resources to pay for that," she added.
Annamma said even if the pipes were replaced, it would take nearly three to four months before supplies could match demand.

Cochin Refineries' spokesman Sanjeev Nair told Reuters that production had come to a halt as the water supply had dwindled to 8,450 kilolitres per day as compared to the refinery's daily demand of 22,750 kilolitre.
"There was no option but to shut down," he said.
But Nair said the closure was temporary, noting that the state government was loosing nearly 30 million rupees per day due to the closure.
Nair said the refinery's crude shipments had not been affected but said a backlog of crude shipments could happen if the problem persisted.
He said the refinery will have to reconsider the modus operandi for some of its future projects.
He said to overcome the water problem the refinery had submitted a proposal with the state goverment to set up its own water supply system.
The refinery has products in stock to provide one week's supply and sufficient ullage to take crude deliveries, he said.
"This is the first time the refinery has closed down because of this reason," he said.
-- Sunil Kataria New Delhi newsroom +91-11 301 2024
